color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
UNIT - tests/unit/, 18 files
state machine, orchestrator, domain pack, prompt pack,
identity resolver, IVR walk, context + brief, matching,
presence + assignment, capture, queue hours, diagrams

div.style: color: rgb(11, 37, 69) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
CONTRACT SUITES - tests/contracts/, 5 files
every adapter for a port must pass the SAME suite, and the
store suite runs three times: in-memory / SQLite / Postgres.
This is what makes a hackathon-day swap safe: the new
adapter either passes or it does not ship. (D75)

div.style: color: rgb(46, 16, 101) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
INTEGRATION - tests/integration/
boots a real app over real HTTP, throws it away,
boots a second on the same storage and asks what it knows.
The only shape that can prove a restart.

div.style: color: rgb(255, 255, 255) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
SCENARIOS - 3 scripted calls, end to end
pattheera_ipd - roadside_motor_claim - anonymous_declined
byte-identical on replay, with expect: blocks checked

div.style: color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
496 tests, about 100 seconds
454 pass + 42 skip with no container;
493 pass + 3 skip with Postgres up — the three
are FK cases a dict cannot have

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
why replays are byte-identical
ManualClock + DeterministicIds are INJECTED (D35).
Nothing calls datetime.now() or makes a random id
on its own, so the same scenario produces the same
output every time — which is what makes golden
comparison possible at all.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 26, 19) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
the gap none of these layers closes by itself (B7).
Every test drove the system through endpoints, and endpoints
tick the dispatcher on the way through — so the suite proved
the ticking WORKED without proving anything CAUSED it. Three
services fired only because time passed, and all three were
driven by nothing. Anything time-driven needs a test in which
only time passes.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
three freshness checks, same argument. Generated diagrams,
the voice-prompt manifest, and the keypad page's embedded menu
data are each regenerated into a temp copy and compared. A
committed artefact that silently falls behind is worse than a
missing one, because it is convincing.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 56, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
grep -rn '# P1:' scripts/
lists every lifecycle step the runner still does by hand.
P3 took the IVR ones over; what is left is the media
gateway, the named agent, and the agent-side rating.
The handover list is executable, not prose. (D36)
